items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:ext-terms at source lines 920-924: the semantic value of the term obtained by substituting t' for x in t, evaluated under an assignment s, equals the value of t evaluated under the assignment that differs from s only at x, where it takes the value of t'. The proof at source lines 926-959 is a structural induction on the term t and it is the substitution lemma of first-order semantics, so it is a real bookkeeping argument rather than a one-step unfolding. The four cases are not symmetric: the constant case is immediate, the variable case other than x needs the observation that the modified assignment agrees with s at that variable, the case t = x needs the definition of the modified assignment at the substituted variable itself, and the composite case needs the induction hypothesis applied simultaneously to all the immediate subterms together with two definitional unfoldings of the value function, arranged with explicit annotations in a displayed chain of equalities. Nothing in the statement indicates which case needs which observation. No result outside the retained text is used.
